blocks.text: With a mostly English-speaking team, it was a practical decision to translate the historical Dutch sources into English. This made the material more accessible, but it also raised questions about cultural translation. The language of the 1930s and 1940s carries meanings, assumptions and social hierarchies that cannot always be transferred directly into modern-day English.

"We tried to preserve the meaning and tone of historical text as much as possible, with the help of reference texts and AI. Translation also confronts temporal distance: for example, the gap between the girls' world and our own. Our aim was not to erase that distance, but to make it readable while keeping its historical specificity visible." — Jaïr

blocks.caption: "Mijnheer" in one of the documents. As of 2026, the word is rarely used in everyday speech, having largely been replaced by "meneer". (Source: Noord-Hollands Archief.)

blocks.text: "Many institutional terms no longer translate comfortably into the present. Descriptions that once appeared clinically neutral now often sound moralising or violent." — Naomi
The podcast is in English, but it was recorded in the Netherlands, with Dutch actors.

"Most of the actors we hired have a Dutch accent in English. We decided the podcast would be in English, but still wanted it to have a Dutch feel, a relation to the real place where the story comes from." — Ari
